title: Tenant-bounded mirror broker and cost-sentinels for shadow traffic
creator: Amina Khurana
description: We need a mirror broker service that allows safe, budget-aware replication of live requests to experimental model variants without affecting production SLAs or tenant billing. The broker must enforce per-tenant budgets/quotas for mirrored traffic, support multiple sampling strategies (stratified, deterministic, adaptive), and isolate mirrored requests to prevent data leakage and downstream side effects. The feature enables long-running shadow runs for quality evaluation and A/B comparison while capping infrastructure spend and avoiding noisy neighbors.
background_and_context: Current ad-hoc shadowing is implemented across gateways and ad hoc proxies. This has led to runaway cost for a few tenants, inconsistent sampling behavior across regions, and operational burden when mirrored requests trigger side effects (e.g., external service calls, billing events). We want a centralized, policy-driven mirror broker that standardizes sampling, implements guardrails, and produces lineage metadata for auditing and rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Mirror broker daemon deployed behind API gateway and reachable via internal mirror endpoint
Per-tenant mirror budget (daily token cap) enforced with hard stop and soft throttles
Sampling strategies supported: fixed-rate, deterministic hashing by tenant+user, and adaptive ramp-up based on error/latency signals
Mirrored requests tagged with immutable metadata (mirror_id, origin_request_id, sampling_reason, replica_model_version)
Shadow requests blocked from making external side-effecting calls by default (outbound call sandboxing flag)
Observability dashboards for mirrored QPS, token consumption, error delta, and cost burn-rate
Automatic fallback: if mirror broker latency > 50ms or error rate delta > 5% vs production, suspend mirroring for affected tenants
End-to-end integration test exercising budget exhaustion, sampling drift, and isolation gates
Conformance with security review: KMS usage for persisted mirror metadata, redact PII in mirrored payloads by default
implementation_steps: 1) Design API contract: POST /internal/mirror with headers X-Mirror-Policy, X-Origin-Request, X-Tenant-ID and documented response codes
2) Implement lightweight broker service in Go with token-bucket per-tenant using Redis for counters and bursts
3) Add sampling engine module supporting stratified & deterministic hashing and an adaptive controller that reads metrics from Prometheus
4) Wire in outbound sandbox: a feature flag that rewrites HTTP clients in mirrored flows to a noop or to a request-capture proxy
5) Add mirror metadata enrichment in transport (mirror_id, sample_policy, ttl, traceparent)
6) Integrate cost-sentinels: periodic job that converts mirrored token usage into dollar burn estimate and posts to billing alert topic
7) Expose control plane: per-tenant policies editable from Console and via internal API with audit logs
8) Build Dashboards and Alerting: burn-rate, mirror-latency, delta-error, budget-threshold warnings
9) Pilot with two internal tenants: test-platform and search-team for 2 weeks with 0.5% fixed sampling and auto-throttle enabled
10) Gradual rollout: enable for cohorts, monitor, then open to broader teams with playbook
testing_plan: Unit tests for sampling logic including deterministic hashing edge cases
Integration tests: mirror flows through gateway -> broker -> replica runtime using test harness
Chaos tests: broker failure, Redis outage, and simulated high latency to verify automatic suspension behavior
Cost-saturation test: generate mirrored traffic to exceed per-tenant daily cap and assert hard-stop and alerting
Security tests: verify PII redaction and that sandboxed flows cannot reach external endpoints in staging
Load test: confirm broker can handle 15k rps of mirrored requests with <10ms additional per-request overhead for proxy routing metadata
runbook_and_playbook: If mirror.broker latency > 200ms: escalate to infra on-call, flip global suspend toggle in Console
If a tenant hits hard cap: notify tenant owners, mark as suspended with reason in UI, open support ticket
If mirrored traffic causes downstream side-effects: toggle sandbox flag on all mirrored flows immediately and roll forward fixes
On cost burn alert: run job to estimate 7-day projection and apply emergency throttles if projection > SLA budget * 1.5
dependencies: ENG-94501 (per-tenant billing meters and billing alerts)
notes: We intentionally separate the mirror broker from runtime routing to keep failure domains small; the broker only returns metadata and an actionable routing hint rather than performing the replication itself when possible.
Adaptive sampling controller design doc: link to Confluence (internal) - confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Mirror+Adaptive+Controller
We will start with tokens measured in 'mirror-token' ~ 1 token per request + token per 1k tokens generated approximation for costs; refine after pilot
